newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Quiet trade on Indian holiday.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Quiet trade on Indian holiday.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) were becalmed on Wednesday ahead of the pricing of State Bank of India's offering on Thursday and a holiday in Bombay.
"There is little inClination to trade," said one trader.
The James Capel Indian GDR Index fell 0.04 points, or 0.06 percent to 65 points, a 8.09 percent premium over the local market.

Among individual stocks, Reliance fell out of favour after rallying to a small premium over the underlying stock on Tuesday and ended off 23 cents on Wednesday at $10.00/$11.00 after having moved up on the back of low volume earlier in the week.
East Indian Hotels was marked up from Tuesday's closing low to end 20 cents higher at $18.75/$19.75.
Arvind Mills fell three cents to $3.40/$3.90 after Peregrine issued a "sell' note on the company.
The key issue for the market is the pricing of State Bank of India on Thursday and the start of trading for the GDR on Friday.
"It appears to have gone quite well," said a trader.
Elsewhere in Asia, the Capel Korea Index fell 0.44 points, 0.62 percent, to 69.28 points, a premium of 28.26 percent over the local market after the Korea Composite Index rose 4.54 points to 794.01.
The Capel Taiwan Index rose 0.03 points to 89.97 points, a premium of 2.69 percent over the local market.
